stories.body: At least six people were killed and 15 wounded in a shooting at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, on Bangkok's northwestern outskirts, Thai authorities said. Police identified the suspected gunman as a 14-year-old student at the school, who was later found dead after allegedly opening fire on teachers and fellow pupils. Reports said three teachers and three students were among those killed. The attack, which prompted students and staff to flee classrooms as police searched the site, has renewed scrutiny of gun access in Thailand following previous school and mass shootings.
stories.headline: Thailand school shooting leaves at least six dead; suspect identified as a 14-year-old student

stories.body: Iran says it is close to finalising an agreement with Oman on shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway that has effectively been closed amid the Iran-US war. Iranian officials said the two countries had agreed coordinates for a commercial corridor and were reviewing a joint statement, though Tehran stressed that a bilateral deal would not by itself make the route safe. The United States has said it would reject any arrangement leaving Iran in control of the strait, while Iranian sources disputed President Donald Trump's assertion that a reopening was imminent and said key details remained unresolved. The strait normally carries about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies.
stories.headline: Iran and Oman say a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is close

stories.body: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey are expected to sign a joint defence agreement in Jeddah as their leaders meet amid regional tensions linked to the war on Iran. Saudi and Turkish sources told media that the foundational terms had been agreed, and that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif would discuss the pact. No government had publicly confirmed a final agreement, and officials cautioned that the meeting could instead result in a more limited joint statement. If concluded, the arrangement could expand the Saudi-Pakistan mutual defence agreement signed in 2025 into a three-country framework.
stories.headline: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey set to sign a joint defence pact in Jeddah

stories.body: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay an additional $567 million after finding that the company created a public nuisance through harms to children on its platforms. The award comes on top of $375 million imposed in an earlier phase of the state case, bringing the total to $942 million. Judge Bryan Biedscheid compared the company to a factory whose harmful effects extend beyond its products, and directed that the new payment go into a fund aimed at reducing future harm. The case stemmed from allegations that Meta's recommendation systems exposed young users to harmful content, sexual exploitation and contact with predators. Meta said it disagreed with the ruling and would appeal.
stories.headline: Meta ordered to pay $567 million in New Mexico child-safety ruling

stories.body: Israeli prosecutors have charged settler Yinon Levy with reckless manslaughter in the July 2025 killing of Palestinian activist Awdah Hathaleen in Umm al-Khair in the occupied West Bank. Levy also faces charges of armed trespassing and malicious property damage after a confrontation sparked by settlers operating an excavator in the village. Prosecutors say Levy cocked his gun and fired toward residents, striking Hathaleen; Levy has denied firing the fatal shot and says he will contest the case. Hathaleen, a teacher and father of three, helped film the Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land. Israeli rights group B'Tselem said this was the first indictment of an Israeli for killing a Palestinian in the West Bank in nearly three years.
stories.headline: Israel charges West Bank settler over killing of Palestinian activist Awdah Hathaleen

stories.body: Extreme heat has broken temperature records across central and eastern Europe, with Slovakia recording a new national high of 42C in Dolné Plachtince and record temperatures also reported in Austria and Hungary. Critically low water in Poland's Vistula River forced the shutdown of the Kozienice and Połaniec coal plants, removing about 1.3GW from the national power system. Drought and heat are also worsening wildfire risks: roughly 500,000 hectares have burned across the EU this year, mainly in Spain and France, while another 292,000 hectares have burned in Ukraine. Officials and environmental groups warned that the conditions are straining communities, infrastructure and energy systems.
stories.headline: Extreme heat breaks temperature records across central and eastern Europe

stories.body: President Donald Trump signed two executive orders intended to further limit birthright citizenship, including an order targeting so-called birth tourism by pregnant visitors. One order expands the categories of non-citizen parents whose US-born children would not automatically receive citizenship, including foreign government employees, members of designated foreign terrorist groups and people accused of seeking citizenship fraudulently. The administration says it is acting under immigration law, but the orders follow the Supreme Court's rejection of Trump's previous effort to curtail the constitutional right. The White House has portrayed birth tourism as a major security concern, while the Migration Policy Institute estimates that 22,000 to 26,000 US births annually may be linked to the practice.
stories.headline: Trump signs executive orders targeting birthright citizenship and birth tourism

stories.body: Republican Representative Andy Ogles lost the Tennessee 5th District primary to former state agriculture commissioner Charlie Hatcher, dealing a setback to President Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson, who had backed Ogles in the closing days of the race. Hatcher benefited from a late endorsement by Governor Bill Lee, stronger fundraising and outside spending, while a newly redrawn district forced Ogles to appeal to unfamiliar voters. Ogles had faced scrutiny over campaign-finance records, claims about his resume and inflammatory social-media posts. Hatcher will face Democratic Columbia Mayor Chaz Molder in November, though the redesigned district strongly favors Republicans.
stories.headline: Trump-backed Representative Andy Ogles loses Tennessee Republican primary

stories.body: A 37-year-old man accused of starting the Old Trails Fire near Spokane, Washington, allegedly told investigators that he planned the blaze for two weeks and selected a day with high winds, low humidity and heat. Court documents say Aaron Farinacci also researched how to make a time-delay ignition device and claimed responsibility for 25 other fires in the area over the past year. The fire is the largest of three around Spokane and has prompted more than 60,000 evacuations while destroying more than 700 buildings. A judge raised Farinacci's bond to $2 million and ordered a competency evaluation; no plea was entered.
stories.headline: Spokane arson suspect charged after allegedly planning wildfire for weeks

stories.body: The US Justice Department has accused Duke University's law school of unlawfully considering race in admissions, saying it used personal essays and first-generation-college status as proxies despite claiming to use race-neutral standards. The department said Black and Hispanic applicants were admitted at higher rates than white and Asian applicants with comparable academic credentials, and noted differences in median LSAT scores among admitted and rejected applicants in 2024 and 2025. The finding is part of the Trump administration's broader campaign against admissions practices after the Supreme Court banned affirmative action in 2023. Duke Law said it was reviewing the letter and remained committed to complying with the law.
stories.headline: Justice Department says Duke Law School illegally considered race in admissions

stories.body: Spain's government is preparing to begin procedures to distribute unaccompanied migrant children from Ceuta among the autonomous communities after the recent mass arrival from Morocco overwhelmed local reception facilities. The conservative People's Party has said regional governments it leads, including those governing with Vox, will comply with the law, although Vox opposes redistribution and argues that children should be returned to Morocco. Authorities and aid groups are still identifying many minors who remain without shelter. Estimates differ sharply: the central government has said about 2,500 people, including around 500 minors, remain in Ceuta, while the local government has cited roughly 6,000 people and more than 860 registered minors.
stories.headline: Spain prepares to distribute unaccompanied migrant children from Ceuta among regions

stories.body: Opposition Islamist and left-wing parties in Morocco are demanding an investigation into deaths during the mass migration crisis at Ceuta, exposing political divisions before September's parliamentary elections. Morocco's government says 11 people died on its territory, while Spanish and Moroccan NGOs estimate that more than 60 died there. Separate figures cited by Spanish authorities and aid groups put the total death toll much higher, with Caminando Fronteras reporting at least 141 deaths in Moroccan and Spanish waters. The crisis involved the irregular entry of more than 72,000 people into Ceuta and has raised questions about how such large crowds reached a heavily monitored border and whether Moroccan controls were deliberately relaxed.
stories.headline: Moroccan parties demand an investigation into deaths in the Ceuta migration crisis

stories.body: King Felipe VI has committed to visit Ceuta after meeting the president of the autonomous city, Juan Jesús Vivas, who described the pledge as a significant gesture of support following the migration crisis. No date has been announced, and any visit would require government approval under Spain's constitutional arrangements. Vivas told the king that between 3,000 and 6,000 migrants remain in Ceuta after the arrival of more than 70,000 people from Morocco, while adult and child reception facilities remain overwhelmed. He called for support from the rest of Spain, rapid action on the overcrowded centers and stronger security at the border.
stories.headline: King Felipe VI pledges to visit Ceuta following meeting with the city's president

stories.body: Spain's Civil Guard is investigating online calls for a possible collective crossing into Ceuta from Morocco on August 15, warning that the risk is real but the scale and organizers remain unknown. An internal assessment found messages circulating on Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram since late July, often sharing the date, departure points and logistical discussion, but said there is no evidence identifying a single organizer, Moroccan government involvement or a criminal network. The report also noted false or misleading claims online about an open border, asylum rights and protections against return. It said preventive action by Morocco and Spanish reinforcements would be decisive in determining whether a crossing takes place.
stories.headline: Authorities investigate a possible new mass crossing into Ceuta on August 15

stories.body: A French-Argentine tourist travelling in Europe has been isolated in Galicia after testing positive for Andes hantavirus following a mild respiratory illness in France. Spain's Health Ministry said the patient was already asymptomatic when he arrived in Spain and was believed no longer contagious, but public-health authorities in Galicia and France are coordinating testing, isolation and contact tracing. French officials confirmed that the infection is the Andes strain of hantavirus. The case follows the end in June of Spain's monitoring of a previous hantavirus outbreak associated with the MV Hondius cruise, in which three people died.
stories.headline: Tourist in Galicia isolated after testing positive for Andes hantavirus

stories.body: One month after an eight-metre sinkhole opened during Barcelona Metro Line 9 works in Sant Gervasi, many residents and businesses remain displaced or face continuing losses. About 300 people were initially evacuated; authorities have cleared residents and businesses in three buildings to return, but around 40% of those affected, including occupants of the four buildings nearest the sinkhole, may have to wait until at least September after another cavity and structural cracks were found. Some residents who have been allowed back remain in hotels because they distrust the safety assurances. Fifteen businesses have been affected, with owners reporting lost income and uncertainty over compensation as technicians continue stabilisation work and investigate the cause.
stories.headline: Residents remain displaced and businesses face losses one month after the Line 9 sinkhole in Sant Gervasi

stories.body: Mossos d'Esquadra have arrested a man in connection with the violent death of another man in Barcelona's Nou Barris district. Police were alerted by the city's municipal police shortly after 12:40 p.m. that a man was badly injured in the street near Carrer de Casals and Carrer d'Almansa in the Verdum neighborhood. Emergency services took him to hospital in critical condition, where he later died. According to reporting by TV3, the attack followed an argument involving three people inside a residential building, during which the victim was stabbed in the face and neck before walking away and collapsing. Investigators have seized a motorcycle that may be linked to the case, which remains under judicial secrecy.
stories.headline: Man arrested over fatal violent attack in Barcelona's Nou Barris district

stories.body: Severe thunderstorms brought intense rain, hail, lightning and strong winds to much of Catalunya, disrupting three Rodalies rail lines and causing localized flooding, power outages and road closures. Rail services were interrupted on the R3 between Vic and Ripoll after a tree fell on the tracks, on the R11 between Maçanet-Massanes and Girona because of a catenary problem, and on the RL4 between Calaf and Manresa due to flooded tracks. Santa Coloma de Farners lost power for nearly an hour and recorded 47.3 litres of rain per square metre, while hail damaged vehicles in the Vall de Bianya. Emergency services received around 400 calls, largely for flooding, fallen branches and structural hazards.
stories.headline: Severe storms and hail disrupt roads and rail services across Catalunya
